question.problem:
Consider the equivalence relation $∼$ on $R,$ defined by $x∼y$ if ${x}^{3}={y}^{3}.$ Which of the following are in the equivalence class $[8]?$

I. $-2$

II. $2$

III. $8$

current_example.problem:
Consider the equivalence relation $\sim$ on $\mathbb{Z},$ defined by $x \sim y$ if $12 \,|\, (x-y).$ Which of the following are in the equivalence class $[9]?$

I. $9$

II. $21$

III. $22$
current_example.worked_solution:
The equivalence class $[9]$ consists of the elements that are equivalent to $9$ under the given equivalence relation. So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}[9] & ={x\in Z\,:\,x∼9} \\  & ={x\in Z\,:\,12\,|\,(x-9)} \\  & ={x\in Z\,:\,x=9+12k,k\in Z} \\  & ={…,-15,-3,9,21,33,…}.\end{aligned}
$$

We see that $9$ and $21$ are in $[9],$ while $22$ is not.

Therefore, the correct answer is "I and II only."
